summary.intent: Investigate the someguy IPNS sidecar state on staging, diagnose its performance issues, upgrade Kubo to v0.40.0, and clean up CI pipeline parallelization.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed someguy's IPNS endpoint as completely non-functional (hanging indefinitely on PUT/GET), reverted staging to delegated-ipfs.dev, upgraded Kubo v0.34.0→v0.40.0 (validated with 83 E2E + 9,100 load test ops), removed someguy from staging, fixed release-please to recognize build commits, and parallelized CI jobs to reduce pipeline critical path.

repo: Someguy's /routing/v1/providers/ works fine but /routing/v1/ipns/ hangs indefinitely — the IPNS delegation is broken in v0.11.1
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL in .env.staging was never actually disabled — a prior 'disable' either didn't persist or was overwritten by a subsequent deploy resetting to compose defaults
docker/ directory with docker-compose files is committed to the repo (not generated by CI) — was confused because the working directory was tests/load/ during search
release-please default config only triggers releases for feat and fix types — build/perf/revert are ignored without explicit changelog-sections config
Grafana Cloud free-tier instance sleeps when idle and returns 503 'Your instance is loading' on wake — provisioning must wait for readiness
CI build job depended on sdk-e2e completing before building — fully sequential critical path: changes → typecheck → test → sdk-e2e → build
Kubo v0.34.0 was referenced in ci.yml, load-test.yml, and e2e.yml service containers — all needed bumping
Alloy monitoring config (alloy-config.river) was scraping someguy metrics and needed cleanup when removing the service

code.finding: Default fallback URL is https://delegated-ipfs.dev when DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env var is not set
test job had typecheck in needs — unnecessary since test builds packages itself; removing it enables parallelism
Throttle bypass requires X-Throttle-Bypass header with THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET — not set in SDK E2E test env, causing 429s during load tests
No changelog-sections configured — added build, perf, revert types so they trigger version bumps

workflow: NODE_ENV=test in shell does not override .env file — NestJS ConfigModule loads .env and wins; must edit the file directly or unset the var
vitest --testPathPattern matches substrings — mixed-workload also matches sustained-load, running all scenarios unintentionally; use anchored patterns
Someguy v0.11.1 is actually a patch ahead of the latest tagged release v0.11.0 — version bumping is not always the answer
Kubo v0.40.x breaking changes are all gateway-related (IPIP-524, IPIP-523) — RPC API users are unaffected
CodeRabbit's 'stability improvements' summary for v0.40.1 was misleading — it was a Windows-only Go toolchain downgrade, irrelevant on Linux

friction: Someguy's IPNS hang required multiple rounds of curl testing (with increasing timeouts) to confirm it was truly non-functional vs just slow
Working directory was tests/load/ causing docker-compose glob searches to fail — had to search from repo root explicitly
Load test 'errors' (74-95% error rate) were misleading — they were SDK-side metrics failures, not HTTP errors; API was returning 200s throughout
Rate limiting (429s) during E2E tests required finding and using the X-Throttle-Bypass mechanism — THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET not documented in test setup
Git history search found no evidence of someguy being disabled — the disable either never persisted or was silently reverted by a deploy
build commit type not triggering release-please was only discovered after merging PR #321 and watching the CI run skip
